title: The Paddock relief band with Sweet Emma and Percy Humphrey
summary: The relief band at the Paddock, how Sweet Emma got her bells, and the rotating cast of horn players.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Oh, yeah, I was playing, uh, let me see, then we, Me and Poison Humphrey, we were just working together. Them the fellas I forgot to mention. See, when we'd be living in the field, Me and Poison Humphrey, we'd be playing together like that, on and off, Em and all of us like that. And we decided to make that band strong, you know, just make, organize it like. Yeah. But Sweet Em and Esma, she used it. And the name first was titled from Miss Valente at the paddock. She's the one made Em use that adopted name of the bell girl.

And Miss Valente gave her that idea. By playing and beating the rhythm with her two foots, she used to relief there on Tuesday nights. Yeah. Play relief nights in the... Oh, yeah. Well, you know, playing the piano is like a man playing a drum with an afterpeat like a stock house. Yeah. They gave her the ideas. And she put bells on her ankles.
Because Bill says, use the bells on your ankles. It's like a rhythm effect. Yeah. That's where that started from.

That time, with that band, was what Rick Howe was playing, Poison. And sometimes we had Piku with us. Yeah. Yeah. Mostly. Then we'd try to get Willie, but Willie was working with Paul Barber and sometimes with Fredrick Coleman, that. And the same block by Sid DeVille at Montegral. But we first started with Piku playing Clown and Poison. And we had a trombone player by the name of, he died not long ago. That man live uptown there. Not Piers? No, not late. What's his name?
His name is a little, not French here. Joe Avery. Joe Avery, yeah. He played a good while with us. Joe Avery.

And Emma and Rick Howe played. Yeah. Then when Piku stood there, then when Piku, I think Piku's out of getting feeling kind of bad. He used to alternate. He'd be with his wildest faces, you know. Sometimes we couldn't get Piku where we might use the answer and then we'd use the Andrew Morgan. Piku?

Oh, Piku. Alphonse Piku, yeah. And we'd get Andrew Morgan or either we'd try to be getting that Willie, because Willie was working with Paul. That one, Willie, I don't know how you come out of Freddie's band, Freddie Coleman's band, my friend. Freddie got Sam Dutra to play Clown and well that showed Willie. He still was working with Paul and sometimes we could get him to come play with that. Yeah. Just that one night, you know. That's it. At the paddock with us, the relief band.
